valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027E diluted EPS in CAD converted to USD at the 2026-11-13 close FX rate of 1 USD = 1.4270 CAD, or 1 CAD = 0.7008 USD, for NYSE: IMO).

bear.driver: Weaker crude/WCS differentials and softer refining crack spreads

base.driver: Mid-cycle oil/refining margins, ~450 kb/d upstream, ongoing NCIB buybacks

bull.driver: Elevated crude prices, tight WCS differentials, strong downstream utilization

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027E EPS of US$10.16, the $128.70 close implies 12.67x P/E; the published Street consensus target (~$116.00 USD) implies 11.42x P/E or US$9.28 EPS at 12.5x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $10.16 (7.9 pp of price return).
valuation.watch_metric: Upstream gross production (kb/d vs. 441-460 kb/d guidance), downstream refinery utilization (91-93% guidance), and NCIB share repurchase pace.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 earnings news release (estimated January 29, 2027) and Form 10-K (estimated February 17, 2027).

analyst_notes: Published Street consensus for IMO (NYSE) sits around $116.00 USD (C$159.55 CAD) with a cautious Hold/Reduce/Underperform tilt from covering firms including RBC Capital (Greg Pardy), TD Cowen (Menno Hulshof), CIBC (Dennis Fong), BMO Capital (Randy Ollenberger), and Scotiabank. The ~10% gap between consensus (~$116) and our base case ($127.00, -1.3% vs. close) reflects analysts applying ~11.4x forward P/E due to valuation concerns after strong share-price appreciation. Individual dated broker notes with exact USD target timestamps were not available in public summaries.
